$comment: File-level counterpart manifest, shared by the storybook-check skill (drift audits) and the storybook-sync skill (triage counterpart lookups). Each mapping ties one upstream file (storybookjs/storybook, branch `next`) to its ported local counterpart. `intentionalDivergences` records accepted, deliberate differences so audits don't re-report them — keep it current: an undocumented divergence is indistinguishable from a bug. Entries with `local: null` have no direct counterpart; their `note` says what to review when the upstream file changes. Packages sync watches only as loose pattern sources (builder-vite, core-webpack) deliberately have no entries here — file-level mappings only make sense where a real port exists.

intentionalDivergences: normalizePath() applied to mockMap keys and resolved requests — pathe and require.resolve disagree on Windows path separators
optional `configDir` plugin option not present upstream
uses compiler.getInfrastructureLogger instead of storybook/internal/node-logger
passes compiler directly to NormalModuleReplacementPlugin.apply; the redundant `as any` assertion is rejected by Rstack 0.7.4 typed lint
resolves the HTML plugin from compiler.options.plugins by constructor name (HtmlRspackPlugin/HtmlWebpackPlugin) instead of importing html-webpack-plugin directly
warn message interpolates `String(error)` instead of upstream's bare `${error}` to satisfy the repo's typed lint (restrict-template-expressions); same output
an `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/unbound-method` comment precedes the `HtmlPlugin?.getCompilationHooks ?? HtmlPlugin?.getHooks` lookup; code is otherwise identical
debug message interpolates `String(error)` instead of upstream's bare `${error}` to satisfy the repo's typed lint (restrict-template-expressions); same output
an `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/await-thenable` comment precedes the `await parseEs(source)` that upstream keeps despite the wrong types; code is otherwise identical

add-vs-change is classified from the built module graph (compilation.fileDependencies) instead of upstream's firstRun heuristic, which misclassifies the first edit of a pre-existing file as `add` when the cold-start watchRun reports no initial file set
builder entry drives Rsbuild's createRsbuild/dev-server lifecycle instead of webpack compiler + webpack-dev-middleware; compare behavior (start/build/bail/corePresets contract), not structure

PREVIEW_BUILDER_PROGRESS ported without the modulesCount cache loop or progress.modules counts — Rspack's ProgressPlugin has no modulesCount estimation option and nothing consumes the cached value (PR #553)
progress value resets between compilations so rebuilds report real progress — upstream's monotonic clamp never resets and pins every rebuild at 1 (deliberate fix over upstream, PR #553)

dev start() adopts the builder-vite non-blocking contract: it returns before the first compile finishes so core listens and prints the URL immediately, and first-compile errors surface via overlay/terminal instead of failing the process — upstream builder-webpack5's blocking start + fail-on-error is dead under current core, which only listens after start() resolves (PR #553)

mocking is appended in builder code immediately after presets.apply('rsbuildFinal') via pluginStorybookMock — this vite-style builder-code position replaces upstream builder-webpack5's overridePresets slot; details are recorded on the custom-webpack-preset.ts mapping
an `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/unbound-method` comment precedes upstream's `const { apply } = await getPresets(...)` destructuring; code is otherwise identical

changeDetectionAdapter(options) follows builder-vite's src/index.ts instead of builder-webpack5: without a started compiler and with options (the headless `storybook tools` path) it returns the headless adapter from change-detection-adapter/headless.ts
expressed as Rsbuild config instead of raw webpack config; also absorbs upstream preview/base-webpack.config.ts and presets/custom-webpack-preset.ts responsibilities
local Rsbuild config inheritance delegates environment selection to pickRsbuildEnvironment, shared with addons; each caller strips via stripInheritedConfig
build.test.esbuildMinify branch not ported: Rsbuild's output.minify.jsOptions only exposes the built-in SWC minimizer, no clean seam to swap in esbuild (mangle:false/keep_fnames ported in PR #549)

prod minify fragment is injected only when the inherited rsbuild.config has no JS minification customization (no minify: false, minify.js, or minify.jsOptions) — upstream minimizes unconditionally, but the inherited-config path (PR #538) is a local-only feature whose minify settings are user-owned (PR #549 review)

prod minifier uses mangle: { keep_fnames, keep_classnames } instead of upstream's mangle: false — same name-preservation goal (docs titles, Show code) with ~26% smaller gzip; known accepted boundary: `const X = class {}` binding-inferred names are still mangled (rare form, docgen displayName covers user source) (PR #549)

SWC env.targets default comes from Rsbuild's browserslist chain (.browserslistrc / overrideBrowserslist) instead of upstream's hardcoded chrome 100/safari 15/firefox 91 floor — upstream hardcodes only because builder-webpack5 has no browserslist integration; explicit user env.targets wins identically on both sides (PR #556)
B1/B11 module rules use Rsbuild's addRules() API, whose prepend ordering keeps user-provided rules later in the merged config so they retain upstream-equivalent precedence (PR #556)

fallback defaults retain the builder's existing browser polyfills while adding upstream's crypto: false, and merge user fallback values last to fix the local ??= all-or-nothing bug while preserving user precedence (PR #556)
optimization.sideEffects: true is applied through Rsbuild's tools.rspack hook instead of raw webpack config (PR #556)
no standalone base config locally — upstream base-webpack.config.ts behaviors (env define, docs/react handling) must surface inside iframe-rsbuild.config.ts

mappings.note: Mocking is an Rsbuild plugin appended in builder code after presets.apply('rsbuildFinal'); this mirrors builder-vite's viteMockPlugin shape while keeping the after-user ordering of builder-webpack5's override slot. The rest of custom-webpack-preset (user webpack config loading, SWC/babel handling) has its semantic parallels reviewed in iframe-rsbuild.config.ts / preview-preset.ts.
intentionalDivergences: core.disableWebpackDefaults is not ported and is a present-day user-facing no-op for this builder: the public main.ts option type-checks in Storybook 10.5.10, but webpack's default-skip has no Rsbuild equivalent and rsbuildFinal runs after intrinsic defaults so cannot emulate it; CRA was the original motivating use case (upstream PR #15062), and supporting the option would require a real pre-default opt-out
Rslint no-control-regex suppression on the sanitization regex — upstream's control-char range is intentional
LoaderContext type imported from webpack via @ts-expect-error because @rsbuild/core does not reexport it
webpack config mutation expressed as rsbuildFinalDocs via mergeRsbuildConfig; docgen loader wiring adapted to Rsbuild tools API
typescriptPresent guard (fall back to plain react-docgen when typescript cannot be resolved) grafted from react-vite's preset onto this webpack-mapped file

mappings.note: Preset glue for the webpack react preset; its responsibilities are distributed across framework-react/src/preset.ts and react-docs.ts. Review changes for behaviors those files should mirror.
Docgen option types; the local parallels live in framework-react/src/types.ts. Review type/option changes for anything the local types should carry.

intentionalDivergences: core expressed as an async PresetProperty that reads frameworkOptions and forwards frameworkOptions.builder as builder options — upstream made core a static object (PR #34260), but iframe-rsbuild.config.ts consumes builderOptions.lazyCompilation/fsCache so the function form is retained (repo-wide idiom across all framework packages)
builder/renderer specifiers wrapped in fileURLToPath — Rsbuild presets take paths, not file:// URLs (repo-wide idiom)

@storybook/react alias is injected through rsbuildFinal with a framework-local createRequire resolution and merged before the inherited config so explicit user aliases win — upstream injects it in the webpack preset before user webpackFinal (upstream PR #18461)

local package is a single framework serving as the Rsbuild analogue of both react-webpack5 and react-vite; audit for behaviors present in the vite variant but missing from both the webpack5 variant and the local file

Docgen handler used by the vite docgen plugin. framework-react/src/loaders/react-docgen-loader.ts carries the equivalent handler logic; review changes against it.

intentionalDivergences: vite plugin wiring (templateCompilation, vueDocgen, vueComponentMeta) replaced by rsbuildFinal in framework-preset-vue3.ts, which returns the vue-component-meta Rsbuild plugin or the vue-docgen-api loader; experimental_docgenProvider/experimental_manifests are re-exported from docgen/preset.ts like upstream
core expressed as an async PresetProperty reading frameworkOptions and forwarding frameworkOptions.builder as builder options; builder/renderer wrapped in fileURLToPath (repo-wide idiom)

framework-vue3 defaults typescript.skipCompiler to true: the default TypeScript wrapper does not check .vue sources and reports TS2307 for .vue imports when no *.vue module shim exists; users who want SFC checking can set main.ts typescript.skipCompiler=false and checkOptions.tsCheckerOptions.typescript.typescriptPath='@esctn/vue-tsc-api'; upstream vue3-vite ships no SFC type check either
typescript option exposes Rsbuild builder TypescriptOptions (ts-checker) instead of upstream's none
VUE_DOCGEN_API_DEPRECATION names framework 'storybook-vue3-rsbuild' instead of '@storybook/vue3-vite'

mappings.note: Ported at v10.6.0. On upstream next this file moved to code/renderers/vue3/src/docgen/preset.ts (storybookjs/storybook e991237e, not in v10.6.0 or v11.0.0-alpha.0), so coverage reports MISSING-UPSTREAM until the pinned @storybook/vue3/preset exports experimental_docgenProvider and experimental_manifests itself. At that point delete this local port and its re-export from preset.ts (otherwise the worker descriptor is registered twice) and drop this entry.

intentionalDivergences: vite plugin adapted as an rsbuildFinal preset applying vue-docgen-loader; compare the docgen behavior (options, file matching), not the plugin mechanics

the loader resolves vue-docgen-api through vue-docgen-loader instead of experimental_vueDocgenEngine().vueDocgenApi(); it is skipped when docgen is false or features.experimentalDocgenServer is true, matching upstream viteFinal gating
aliases vue$ (exact match) where upstream vue-template.ts aliases vue — equivalent under Rspack resolve semantics

framework-vue3 keeps the vueDocgenOptions addon-docs preset scan because it is a user-supplied options channel still documented upstream at addons/docs/docs/frameworks/VUE3.md:47-58; Storybook core preserves addon options, so removing it would break documented configuration

the Vite transform plugin becomes an Rsbuild plugin: api.transform with a function `test` carrying upstream's include/exclude filter, and resourceQuery: { not: /./ } for rspack-vue-loader's `?vue&type=script` sub-requests

the exclude list also drops builder-rsbuild's storybook-stories.js and storybook-config-entry.js virtual entries (upstream excludes /virtual: ids) and node_modules, which Vite dev never transforms because it pre-bundles dependencies

the default export binding is probed as `__exports__` (rspack-vue-loader) or `_sfc_main` (unplugin-vue); upstream's imported-`_sfc_main` detection (Vite production output) and the non-SFC `export default` -> `_sfc_main` rewrite have no rspack counterpart and are dropped, so a non-SFC default export (no local binding) is skipped

handleHotUpdate becomes a watchRun hook that calls checker.updateFile for the matching ids in compiler.modifiedFiles; no module invalidation or full reload is needed because Rspack's own HMR re-runs the transform for changed modules

no magic-string: the transform is append-only, so returning the code keeps the incoming source map; the empty and error paths return the source unchanged because Rsbuild's TransformResult has no undefined

localOnlyFiles.$comment: Local files with no storybook upstream origin — listed so coverage audits know they are expected. The react-docgen-typescript plugin is vendored from the external vite-plugin-react-docgen-typescript project, adapted to Rsbuild. headless.ts and preset.ts follow builder-vite (change-detection-adapter/headless.ts and preset.ts); preset.ts is kept as a re-export of preview-preset.ts rather than merged into it so preview-preset.ts stays 1:1 with builder-webpack5's presets/preview-preset.ts while dist/preset.js satisfies the headless `<builder dir>/preset.js` lookup; builder-vite has no file-level mappings, see the top-level $comment.
